Judge: B is better in all 4 pairs. Two B frames carry a commercial game's watermark, so it was obvious which source was which, but I judged only what is visible on screen. The A frames share real strengths: decent cumulus skies, warm sunlight and reasonably detailed shophouse facades. They share the same defects too. Streets are nearly empty, with large areas of bare asphalt in the foreground. The supertrees always render as glowing pink and white wireframes that read as placeholders, and landmarks are simplified grey stand-ins. Extreme wide-angle framing stretches the edges. The aerial view (pair 4) is mostly untextured beige boxes, and the lighting has weak contrast and little aerial perspective, so the low-sun shots never deliver long, readable cast shadows or haze. The B frames are older technology, with softer ground textures and simpler midday light in places. Even so, they consistently show authored detail at every depth, life (people, cars, aircraft), strong silhouettes and atmospheric depth. Pair 2 was the closest: A's sky and bounce light look more modern, but its placeholder assets cost it on believability. Only pair 4 B genuinely wowed me. The highest-leverage fixes for A are: populate the near and mid-ground with vehicles and pedestrians that cast sun-aligned shadows; replace the wireframe supertrees and grey landmark stand-ins with finished assets; give blockout buildings real facades; and add distance haze so contrast drops with depth.
